mstts:express-as.prosody:
As we wrap up, think about what the journey of the Wright brothers really means for you. Their story isn’t just about building the first airplane—it's a living, breathing blueprint for anyone who’s ever dared to dream big, roll up their sleeves, and keep going, even when the world isn’t paying attention.
What can we take with us from their legacy? Curiosity and a hunger to learn can shine brighter than any diploma. Real breakthroughs come from steady, persistent work—and from leaning on others, not just going it alone. Setbacks? They're not dead ends. They're just the rough patches on the road to progress.
And, maybe most importantly, it’s the support of family and community—the folks who cheer you on quietly—that often fuels the greatest triumphs. Integrity and responsibility count just as much as skill or recognition.
So, if you ever find yourself staring down a challenge that feels just too big, picture the Wright brothers in their little workshop—tinkering, arguing, laughing, and refusing to give up. Let their journey remind you: greatness isn’t just for a lucky few. It’s built, day by day, through small acts of courage and resilience.
Trust your questions. Lean on those who believe in you. And when the world doubts, let your work do the talking.
The sky? As the Wright brothers showed us, it's not the limit. It's just the beginning.
